newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-MYSTERY STILL SURROUNDS MONTGOMERIE WITHDRAWAL.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MYSTERY STILL SURROUNDS MONTGOMERIE WITHDRAWAL.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie's sudden withdrawal from the European Tournament Players' Championship (TPC) was still shrouded in mystery on the eve of the event starting on Thursday.
At the same time it was revealed home favourite Bernhard Langer also came close to pulling out, while Severiano Ballesteros, who seemed to be the biggest doubt, declared himself "fully fit".
European number one Montgomerie may now enter next week's English event, but there was little amplification from his manager on Wednesday why he is not in Germany.
"Colin withdrew on Tuesday for personal reasons. This is a private matter and it will remain so, but he is considering playing next week's European Grand Prix instead," said Guy Kinnings.
Langer was in pain from the 16th hole in last Sunday's third round of the PGA at Wentworth, England, jarring his right-hand ring finger and causing a recurrance of ligament trouble.
"It hurt very badly right after playing a shot out of the rough," said Langer, who seeks his third win at this Gut Kaden course in six years and a third win of this year, having had a barren 1996.
"I was very close to not playing here but the injury has happened before and I knew how to treat it. So I am fit again to play."
Ballesteros is to play after a recurring back injury which kept him out of the PGA.
"Before playing the second round at Wentworth last week I felt a lttle pinch in my back. By the time I walked to the practice green I couldn't even bend so I couldn't hit putts," he said
"I went to the physio for massage but it was too painful. Then I had a pain-killing injection but that didn't work so I decided to give myself three days rest. Right now I feel good enough to play."
Northern Irishman Darren Clarke, joint second to Ian Woosnam at Wentworth on Monday, also nearly pulled out of the TPC but changed his mind on the advice of his manager.
Clarke has been promised a Ferrari 355 by his club suppliers if he gets into the European Ryder Cup team and also wins at least two matches.

But Clarke, who is halfway to achieving his sponsor's targets after clinching his Valderrama place on Monday and rising to third in the European points table, has jumped the lights on his backers over owning a Ferrari.
Fast car enthusiast Clarke bought a second hand Ferrari Testarossa from a garage close to Wentworth on Tuesday with some of his 82,000 pounds ($133,000) prize as PGA joint runner-up.
